carbon_policy_signal.item: EU methane reporting rules delayed two years under US pressure; COP31 climate talks collapse without fossil fuel phase-out agreement.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Delay weakens EU climate stringency and signals global fossil fuel phase-out ambition failure. Reduces long-term demand destruction for gas and coal, pressuring EUA forward curve into 2027.

freshness_caveat: Coal data 332 days stale (as_of 2025-12-26); Clean Dark 327 days stale (as_of 2025-12-31). Dispatch margin assessment and thermal merit-order positioning rely on these gaps. TTF, DE Power, GB Power, Storage, Renewable Share, and EUA current as of 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-23.
risk_flags: EU storage 17.5pp below 5-yr seasonal — refill pace will drive H2 2027 power risk; currently 68.89% full vs historical norms.
EUA extended 2.3σ below 50d trend (32.65 EUR/tCO2, -5.14% weekly) — COP31 fossil fuel phase-out failure and methane rule delays weaken medium-term ETS demand drivers.
GB Power at 207.69 EUR/MWh (92nd pctile) while DE Power 195 EUR/MWh (85th pctile) — structural GB premium reflects LNG import reliance and cross-channel constraint.
Coal at 96 USD/t (8th pctile, 332 days stale) — data gap limits near-term dispatch margin assessment; last signal shows thermal compression into spring 2026.

base.summary: Tight storage backdrop persists; GB Power holds elevated premium; EUA consolidates near 32.5 EUR/tCO2 pending methane rule detail.

downside.summary: Milder-than-normal weather or wind recovery lifts renewables; EUA decline extends on policy uncertainty confirmation; thermal call fades. Power spreads compress.

upside.summary: Cold front or additional Russia sanctions escalation; thermal dispatch extends; storage refill pace slows. TTF and GB Power rally on heating demand spike.

themes: GB Power premium sustained by tight EU storage backdrop
Carbon policy uncertainty pressures EUA forward curve post-COP31 collapse
EU methane rules delay bullish for gas supply, bearish for power decarbonisation premium
Russia sanctions escalation supports TTF geopolitical risk premium
top_drivers: GB Power premium sustained by storage -17.5pp below seasonal and LNG import reliance amid Russia sanctions escalation.
EUA weakness driven by COP31 fossil fuel phase-out collapse and EU methane rules delay — signals weakened medium-term decarbonisation ambition and ETS demand.
Renewable share collapsed 45% daily to 21st pctile; thermal call window open — watch for weather reversal or wind recovery to reset merit order.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 92nd percentile amid storage -17.5pp below seasonal; EUA extended 2.3σ below trend as COP31 collapse signals weakened climate ambition and delayed EU methane rules.

watchlist.why: COP31 collapse without fossil fuel phase-out agreement pressures Cal+1 and Cal+2 decarbonisation premium; weakened climate stringency signals multi-year EUA downside.
US storage 2% above 5-yr average reduces LNG export urgency; combined with EU sanctions escalation and methane rule delay, arbitrage value softens near-term EU import incentive.
GB at 92nd pctile vs DE at 85th pctile; sustained premium signals cross-channel constraint tightness and LNG import premium; watch for winter demand destruction or interconnector maintenance.
Renewable share fell 45.09% daily to 30.63% (21st pctile, 1 day old); weather-driven collapse suggests multi-day thermal call window; next cold front or wind recovery critical for merit-order shift.

Two-year delay signals policy retreat; impacts long-cycle investment in carbon capture and power plant retrofit — watch for delayed coal phase-out announcements that extend thermal merit-order duration.

watchlist_dated.name: COP31 fossil fuel re-negotiation timeline announced
watchlist_dated.why: Failed phase-out agreement leaves window for revised commitment; timing and binding language will set EUA curve repricing trajectory into 2027.

watchlist_dated.name: EU methane rules finalized detail — January 2027 delay confirmation
watchlist_dated.why: Confirms two-year delay; allows market to price in longer-cycle gas support and reduced climate stringency drag on power spreads.
